title: jml-automation configuration
description: GENERATED FILE. Edit src/config/schema.ts and run `npm run generate`.

version.description: Config format version. Bumped only for a breaking change.

name.description: Organisation name, used in notifications and the leaver auto-reply.

primaryDomain.description: The domain a canonical address is expressed in.

aliasDomains.description: Comma-separated domains that route to the same mailboxes. Two systems keyed on different domains for one person is how identity joins silently diverge.

timezone.description: IANA zone. ALL date-only arithmetic happens in it; never in UTC.

itTeamSignature.description: Sign-off line on notifications sent to a person.

mode.description: dry-run plans and reports without touching a provider. It is the default, and the demo runs in it.

armedActions.description: Which actions may really happen. An action absent from this list records not_armed rather than running, so arming happens one action at a time.

senderMailbox.description: The mailbox outbound mail is sent AS. Delegated authority is granted for this address specifically.

managerOnDay0.description: Tell the leaver's manager on day 0 that offboarding has started.

adapter.description: Which HR source to read: HiBob, a JSON fixture, a CSV file, or a Google Sheet shared with the service account.

minPlausibleHeadcount.description: REQUIRED, no default. A snapshot smaller than this aborts the run. A truncated read looks exactly like a company where everybody left, and the cost of that mistake is suspending the whole staff, so an adopter states their own floor rather than inheriting a guess.

exitRenamePatterns.description: Regular expressions matching the address an HR system renames a leaver to. A match means the address is an alias on the same person, never a new identity.

serviceUserId.description: Service user id, as a secret reference.

serviceToken.description: Service user token, as a secret reference.

pageSize.description: Page size for the paged read.

fields.description: Where each field lives in the HR payload.

path.description: The CSV file, for adapter csv.

spreadsheetId.description: The sheet id from its URL, for adapter sheet. Share the sheet with the service account address as a viewer.

range.description: The tab name, or an A1 range such as People!A1:Z. The first row is the headings.

dateFormat.description: The one format every date in the table is in. A value in any other format refuses the whole read.

maxAgeHours.description: Refuse a table last changed longer ago than this. For a sheet it needs the read-only Drive scope as the service account.

inScopeValues.description: Values of the inScope column that mean IT provisions for this person.

hrisId.description: A stable id that never changes, even when a name or address does.

primaryEmail.description: The work address, as the account was created.

displayName.description: Full name, if the table has one column for it.

managerEmail.description: The manager's work address: files go to them on day 6.

personalEmail.description: Where a starter temporary password goes.

lastWorkingDay.description: Last day in. Access stops the day after. A leaver keeps their row with this filled in.

terminationDate.description: Contract end date, if different from the last working day.

inScope.description: Whether IT provisions accounts for this person. Blank or unmapped means yes.

table.description: Required when adapter is csv or sheet.

adapter.description: Local SQLite: the default people store.
One Notion database as the people store.

token.description: Internal integration token, as a secret reference.

peopleDatabaseId.description: Database id holding one row per person.

properties.description: Map from this toolkit’s field names to your property names.

statusValues.description: Map from lifecycle status to your select options.

readOnly.description: Never write to the database. Reads, counts, `jml store verify` and every dry run work; every write refuses; a missing property is read as empty rather than added. For a database another automation owns, such as a shadow run beside a live estate.

adapter.description: A spreadsheet as the people store.
In-memory store for the demo and for dry-run rehearsal. Nothing persists.

`jumpcloud` (setup 1.0a) puts a JumpCloud account in front of Google. `none` (setup 1.0b) makes the Google account the only account: day 0 closes it with a random password and a sign-out, starters get their temporary password on Google, and there is no device inventory, so every deletion says none was checked.

baseUrl.description: Some tenants answer only on the console host and return 404 on the other one for every request, valid key or not.

apiKey.description: Organisation API key, as a secret reference.

consoleUrl.description: Where a starter signs in for the first time. Printed in the password and welcome messages.

poolUserEmail.description: Spares account a returned device is rebound to. Null disables the rebind.

serviceAccountJson.description: The whole service account key file, as a secret reference. `file:/path/to/key.json` is the usual form.

adminEmail.description: The admin this service account impersonates for directory, licensing and transfer calls.

customer.description: List by customer, never by one domain: a per-domain list silently misses every account on an alias domain.

licenceProductIds.description: Products searched when revoking a licence.

applications.description: What is handed over. The application id is resolved at run time, never hard-coded.

fallbackRecipient.description: Used when no manager resolves. Null parks the row for a person to decide.

pollTimeoutMinutes.description: How long one run waits before leaving the transfer to be re-polled by the next run.

terminationLookbackDays.description: A leaving date older than this parks the row instead of acting on it. This is the backstop against a stale record being treated as a fresh departure.

maxDay0PerRun.description: Circuit breaker. More day-0 candidates than this aborts the WHOLE run rather than processing the first few, because a sudden crowd of leavers is a data fault far more often than a redundancy round.

maxAttemptsPerLeg.description: After this many failures a leg parks the row for a person.

transferDay.description: Days after suspension that files are handed over.

deleteDay.description: Days after suspension that accounts are deleted.

deletion.description: `never` suspends and hands over, then keeps both accounts. Day 7 is not scheduled at all: no run deletes a retained leaver, reads their devices, or reports a failure over them; the report counts them as retained. Close a row by hand with `jml leaver tombstone` once you have dealt with the accounts. `never` refuses `delete` in armedActions, because the two contradict each other.

revokeLicences.description: `all`, or a list of SKU ids to revoke.

deleteGoogleUser.description: False stops at suspension so the mailbox can be archived by hand.

requireOperatorAck.description: Require a human acknowledgement before any deletion.

requireTransferBeforeDelete.description: Refuse deletion until the file handover is confirmed complete.

bodyHtml.default:
${displayName} no longer works at ${orgName}.

Please contact ${managerName} at ${managerEmail}.

directBindingsOnly.description: NOT overridable. Membership of a group that grants access to a machine is not custody of it, so only a direct binding blocks a deletion.

failClosed.description: NOT overridable. A gate that cannot be read blocks. Reading an error as "no devices" is how an account gets deleted while the machine is still out there.

leadWorkingDays.description: Activate this many working days before the start date, so the temporary password reaches the manager in time. Weekends and the dates in holidays are skipped.

graceDays.description: Somebody who started more than this many days ago with no activation recorded is an existing employee, not a starter: not selected, not announced, and their manager is not nudged. On a fresh people store every employee looks like a starter otherwise. Name a person with --hris-id to activate them regardless.

holidays.description: ISO dates that are not working days. Kept as data rather than a national calendar URL, because the toolkit must not depend on somebody else's endpoint being up on the morning a starter arrives.

maxActivationsPerRun.description: More candidates than this are reported and held for the next run rather than all being activated at once. A crowd of joiners is a data fault far more often than a hiring round.

gate.description: What has to happen before an eligible person is activated. none: nothing. manual: somebody runs `jml joiner approve`. ticket: a ticket raised on the starter form opens it, through the configured ticketing adapter (Suptask ships), and `jml joiner approve` still works by hand.

targetOrgUnitPath.description: Google organisational unit to move the account into on activation, for example the one whose sign-in is delegated to the identity provider. Blank skips the move.

skuId.description: The SKU to assign on activation. Blank skips licensing, and the welcome email is withheld if the mailbox is not ready anyway.

tries.description: How many times to re-read the account waiting for the mailbox.

itSupportEmail.description: Always receives a copy of the temporary password, so it is never lost when the other recipients are unusable.

temporaryPasswordLength.description: Length of the generated temporary password.

adapter.description: Which ticketing system. none disables every ticketing feature.

apiToken.description: Workspace API token, as a secret reference.

queueId.description: The inbox tickets are raised in.

requesterId.description: The chat user id automated tickets are raised as, usually the IT owner.

starterFormId.description: The new-starter form. Only a ticket raised on this form may open the activation gate.

leaverFormId.description: The form leaver tickets are raised on. Blank raises them with no form.

firstNameField.description: Form field label holding the first name.

lastNameField.description: Form field label holding the surname.

emailField.description: Form field label holding the work address, if the form asks for one. Matched before the name.

personalEmailField.description: Form field label holding a personal address. Written to the person when present.

nudgeManager.description: Ask the manager to raise the starter form when a joiner is detected and the gate is closed. Once per person.

dayBeforeReminder.description: Remind the manager once, the day before the start date, if the gate is still closed.

leaverTicket.description: Raise a ticket when a leaver becomes a day-0 candidate, so the platforms IT does not administer have somewhere to be worked through.

formInstruction.description: One sentence telling a manager how to raise the starter form. Printed in the nudge and the reminder.
formInstruction.default: In Slack, run /suptask and choose the new-starter form.

enabled.description: Tell each platform owner in the register when somebody leaves.

goLiveDate.description: Required when enabled. Nobody whose leaving date is before this is ever notified, so switching the feature on cannot blast every owner about every leaver in the history.

lookbackDays.description: A leaver older than this is not picked up, so a register that gains an owner later does not reopen old departures.

adapter.description: Where the register is read from. A file export is the reference; other sources are later adapters.

path.description: CSV with a header row, or JSON. Required when enabled.

ownerColumn.description: Header of the owner-address column. Several addresses may share a cell.

handlingColumn.description: Header of the column saying how offboarding is handled. A value of Retired skips the row.

dispositionDefault.description: What happens to a device when nobody says otherwise.

windows.description: Command trigger name. Null refuses handover on this platform.

darwin.description: Command trigger name. Null refuses handover on this platform.

linux.description: Command trigger name. Null refuses handover on this platform.

name.description: Agent name, echoed in the removal receipt.

services.description: Service names to stop and remove.

uninstallDisplayNames.description: Exact uninstall display names. Anchored, never a substring match.

agents.description: The agents a handover removes, and the receipt keys the script must report back.

agentQuietMinutes.description: Last contact must be frozen this long before a device record is deleted, so the removal is confirmed by silence rather than by an exit code.

staleContactWarnMin.description: Preflight warns when a device has not been heard from for this long.

forbidGroupBoundCommands.description: NOT overridable. A trigger fires on every association the command holds, so a group-attached uninstaller strips the whole fleet.

purgeTelemetryHistory.description: Irreversible. Requires an explicit acknowledgement at the call site as well.

holdMs.description: How long to hold the association after firing. A short hold loses the work on any device that was not connected at that instant.

timeoutMs.description: Give up waiting for a receipt. Never read a timeout as success.

url.description: Optional host-inventory API. Null disables the adapter.

adapters.description: Where notifications go. Console is the default so the first run needs no credential.

templatesDir.description: A folder of your own message wording. A file named like a built-in template (day0-manager.md, joiner-welcome.md and so on) replaces it; the rest keep the built-in text. Checked at start-up: an unknown file name or a placeholder the message does not supply refuses to start.

weeklyReraiseDay.description: A standing problem is re-raised once on this weekday. Once, not on every run of that weekday: a weekday test is true for all of it.

botToken.description: Bot token, as a secret reference.

itChannelId.description: Channel the IT summary is posted to.

itMailbox.description: Mailbox the IT summary is sent to.

minimisePii.description: Store addresses as a salted hash. An audit log is kept for years and does not need to be a staff directory.

salt.description: Hash salt. Required when minimisePii is true.

dir.description: Directory for the append-only log files.

enabled.description: Also push audit rows to a log aggregator.

authHeader.description: Authorization header value, as a secret reference.

healthchecksPingUrl.description: Dead-man ping URL. The URL is itself the credential, so it is a secret reference. Pinged only after a notification is proven delivered.

azure.description: Reserved. The interface exists; nothing runs.

slackScim.description: Reserved. The interface exists; nothing runs.

bind.description: Where the sidecar listens. Not published to the host in the shipped compose file.

token.description: Bearer token for the sidecar. At least 32 bytes; compared in constant time.
